task: DOC-004 (G0 task 4) - engine/editor/storage contract, runtime placement and per-operation evidence
read_before_quoting: This file is not proof that any engine executes in any runtime. Every row carries its own evidence_level and every format summary repeats its counts, so a claimed runtime cannot be read as proven by adjacency.

The DOC-003 six-browser open/edit/save/reopen flows are still not accepted as a whole. UNI-667 owns them. Scoped subordinate cycles in scoped_editor_cycles are real and must not be denied, but they do not raise a preferred-runtime row to proven and do not set runtime_chosen. The 11-case adapter run is real DOC-003 engine-host behavior over loopback and the six canonical fault cases use real DOCX/HTTP engine behavior with modeled Go/storage/commit. Neither is product browser, production service, or placement proof; neither changes evidence_level or runtime_chosen.
Entries marked proposed_g0_output are new G0 design decisions, not existing deployed resources, directories or feed URLs.
A pending row is a blocker with an owner, never a silent downgrade to unsupported. Per Q1-B an upstream capability the web build cannot run yet stays in the requirement set.

evidence_levels.proven: A run exists whose command, environment, fixture and artifact are recorded and repeatable.
evidence_levels.source_read: Source at the pinned commit was read and the symbol exists as written. This proves a symbol, never behaviour.
evidence_levels.pending: No implementation path is proven: a dependency is missing, an adapter must be written, or no run exists. Must not be presented as working.

counting_rule: evidence_level is per operation. A format with one proven operation and five pending operations has one proven row, not a proven runtime. No format in this map is proven end to end.

runtime_kinds.browser: The UniWork web page behind an injected host adapter.
runtime_kinds.worker: Off-main-thread context in the browser host.
runtime_kinds.native_desktop: A process the desktop host owns. Filesystem and native handles stay in that host and never reach the browser API.
runtime_kinds.internal_service: The private Office Engine Service beside UniWork, reached only by Go, never by a browser.
runtime_kinds.none: No engine: file I/O, text handling or host UI only.

versioning_and_rollout.negotiation: The client advertises contract_version, protocol_version and its engine build. Go compares them against the stored document_versions.engine_* columns before a job is created. A mismatch is a typed refusal (engine_incompatible, protocol_mismatch or contract_mismatch), never a silent downgrade.
versioning_and_rollout.rolling_update: An older engine keeps serving documents whose recorded engine version it can still read; a new engine version is introduced behind a flag. A run against an incompatible engine is refused before bytes are written, so the stored current version never moves.
versioning_and_rollout.rollback: Rolling back to the previous engine build must still read every draft and every committed version. Drafts are preserved in the account draft store independently of the engine build, so a rollback cannot lose a draft; a base-version mismatch on recovery surfaces as a conflict, never as silent overwrite (DOC-005 owns the recovery path).
versioning_and_rollout.fixture_replay: Every engine, adapter or protocol version change reruns the DOC-003 fixtures and the DOC-005 fault harness before rollout. The replay is the gate, not the version bump.

proposed_layout: packages/office-contracts/ holds versioned request/result/error schemas and fixture-independent types only.

packages/office-engine-upstream/<module>/ holds selected pinned upstream source, patches, LICENSE and NOTICE inside this monorepo; no sibling checkout, symlink, private registry, or ../genoffice dependency.

packages/office-engine-browser/ exposes browser-safe worker entry points; packages/office-engine-node/ contains Node/native-only entry points. Do not re-export Node, Electron, canvas, or native bindings through the browser entry.

services/office-engine/ owns the private engine service and native sidecars; server/internal/officeengine/ is the Go transport client; server/internal/service/documents/ owns authorization, version, quota, and commit orchestration.
apps/web/platform/ injects host adapters; packages/views/ may depend on @uniwork/core and @uniwork/ui, while core/ui do not import the engine package or app host.
source_and_patch.patch_source_of_truth: Pin upstream commit and source-manifest hashes; store the reviewed patch series beside the vendored module and verify clean-checkout replay. G0 has no tested final package names or patch replay.
source_and_patch.public_entry: Export only typed document operations and versioned protocol contracts from the browser-safe package facade; keep internal service, storage path, Node, Electron, and sidecar APIs private.
source_and_patch.dependency_direction: views -> core + ui; web platform -> injected adapter; Go document service -> private engine client -> private engine service. The engine receives bounded bytes and operation input, never authority to choose a tenant, user path, object key, or database mutation.

version_and_catalog.rule: Keep the shared UniWork catalog versions. Prove compatibility at G2/G3 with clean install, typecheck, build, and browser fixtures; no G0 catalog bump or duplicate React/TipTap tree.

private_service_job_resource_cleanup.authority: Go owns authentication, workspace/organization authorization, quota, idempotency, deadline, and document-version checks before job creation; the engine service is private and receives a scoped operation grant plus bounded bytes.
private_service_job_resource_cleanup.job: Persist job/idempotency and terminal state in G1-owned storage; transitions are accepted -> running -> completed|failed|timed_out|cancelled. A retry with the same key/payload replays; a changed payload conflicts; incompatible contract/protocol/engine refuses before job creation.
private_service_job_resource_cleanup.resource: Enforce input/output byte caps, operation allowlists, bounded concurrency, deadline, memory/temp quotas, and per-job isolated staging. The engine cannot access arbitrary host paths, network destinations, or business tables.
private_service_job_resource_cleanup.commit: Engine output remains staged. Go recomputes the output digest and length, writes the immutable object before the database transaction, then commits version, audit/outbox, and idempotency state atomically; an uncommitted object is tracked for reconciliation.
private_service_job_resource_cleanup.cleanup: Cancellation/timeout/crash must not advance current_version. G1 reconciles service-owned staged objects/orphan ledger; G2 must prove process/temp-tree cleanup. Current evidence cannot guarantee removal of engine-local staged bytes after cancel/deadline or durable job state after parent restart.
private_service_job_resource_cleanup.failure: Return stable typed errors. Preserve original and current version on engine-down, timeout, malformed output, checksum/length mismatch, or cleanup uncertainty; no silent fallback, overwrite, or version downgrade.

upgrade_rollback.rollout: Introduce new engine build behind a disabled-by-default flag and explicit supported contract/protocol range; replay the exact DOC-003 fixture and DOC-005 failure suites before routing any job.
upgrade_rollback.migration: G1 stores engine build and protocol metadata per immutable version; never rewrite existing bytes during engine upgrade.
upgrade_rollback.rollback: Keep the prior service/build able to read committed and draft versions. Disable the new flag and route compatible jobs to the previous build; if it cannot read a version, refuse with typed incompatibility and preserve the stored bytes/draft.
upgrade_rollback.proof: No product upgrade, rollback, multi-version reader, or feature-flag path is implemented by this G0 candidate.
